call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer:
Investments in sustainable business equipment and related buildings that make Groningen's process and manufacturing industry greener or more circular.
The investment must add value to the shift to green chemistry, circular and biobased industry, biotechnology or 'net zero' industry, by aiming at one of these:
- producing and using green hydrogen as a feedstock in industrial chains (not for energy)
- using raw materials of biological origin
- high-grade reuse of products, waste or raw materials, without downcycling
- net zero industry that makes technology needed for the energy transition, such as batteries, solar panels, heat pumps or electrolysers
The need is regional and industrial: the province wants a future-proof industrial cluster under the Nationaal Programma Groningen (a national programme for the region's future after gas extraction).
cards.sources:
Subsidieregeling Investeren in Toekomstbestendige Industrie 2025.pdf · pp. 1-3 · Overwegende dat; Artikel 1 (k, p); Artikel 2 Doel; Artikel 5; Artikel 7, lid 1-2

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
A greener, more circular industrial cluster with new jobs, CO2 reduction and a stronger regional economy.
Projects are scored on a new economic perspective in the four fields, a stronger regional economic structure and CO2 reduction towards a climate-neutral EU in 2050 (30 points); on training days, HR policy and cooperation with education (25); on jobs created or kept (25); and on innovation, cross-over between regional strengths and reduced dependence on fossil fuels and feedstocks (20). Greening the production process means it becomes more energy-efficient or less polluting, which the explanatory note links to a 40% CO2-reduction requirement. Projects may not reduce the applicant's number of jobs.

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer:
Process and manufacturing companies (NACE section C) established in, or moving to, the regional-aid area of Groningen; each company applies for its own investment.
- Large companies: only new establishments or diversification of an existing site
- SMEs (small and medium-sized enterprises): also expansion of capacity or full transformation of the production process
Industrial services, waste processing and biofuels with a blending obligation older than two years are excluded. The call suits manufacturers of energy-transition equipment, green-chemistry and biobased firms, and hydrogen-feedstock users.
cards.sources:

cards.title: Innovation
cards.question: How new must the project be, and in what must it innovate?
cards.answer: The investment need not be a new technology, but innovation is scored: the innovative character of the project (10 points) and its cross-over impact on more than one regional knowledge strength (5). The investment itself is in proven equipment and buildings that are new, apart from exceptions for SMEs and takeovers.

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer:
The investment is put into real production at the company's site in Groningen and must stay in operation there for five years after completion.
For a large company changing its production process, eligible costs must exceed the depreciation of the related assets over the previous three tax years; for diversification, they must be at least 200% of the book value of reused assets.

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer: My judgement: the investments this call supports, such as electrolysers for feedstock hydrogen, electrified green-chemistry processes and new factories for batteries or electrolysers, would add large electricity demand to Groningen's industrial cluster, which TenneT must connect and which could offer flexibility. Knowing about these projects early helps TenneT plan connections and talk to future large customers about flexible contracts. TenneT cannot take part itself: only companies in the process and manufacturing industry (NACE section C) may apply, and the regulation, through article 13 of the EU General Block Exemption Regulation, excludes regional aid for energy production, storage, transmission, distribution and infrastructure.
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
Up to EUR 7.5 million per project, for projects of at least EUR 2.5 million (EUR 1 million on the Zernike campus), from a EUR 9.2 million budget.
- Total project size: eligible costs of at least EUR 2,500,000, or EUR 1,000,000 on the Zernike campus in Groningen city; no maximum
- Grant request: up to EUR 7,500,000 per project, within the maximum regional aid allowed
- Funding form: a share of the purchase price of buildings and sustainable equipment (or the purchase value under financial lease)
cards.sources: Subsidieregeling Investeren in Toekomstbestendige Industrie 2025.pdf · pp. 3-4 · Artikel 6, lid 3f-g; Artikel 8; Artikel 11 Subsidieplafond; Artikel 12, lid 3-4

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
The rate depends on company size, and is 10% for any project above EUR 50 million.
- Small company: up to 30% of eligible costs
- Medium-sized company: up to 20%
- Large company: up to 10%
- Projects with eligible costs above EUR 50 million: up to 10%
- Co-financing conditions: at least 25% of eligible costs from own funds or external financing free of any public support, such as share capital or subordinated loans
- Evidence required: financing must be fully closed, shown with legally binding documents from financiers; an uncommitted term sheet is accepted at application but must become binding within the 22-week decision period

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: an electronic application to SNN through www.snn.nl with a project plan and all annexes listed on the website; budget goes first come, first served by the day, hour and minute of a complete application.
- Stage 1 — Application: until 31 December 2026, 23:59 on the SNN page (the deadline was extended from 30 June 2026)

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
Start within 6 months of the grant and complete by 1 July 2029.
- Required start: within 6 months of the grant decision (a longer term may be set), and no contracts with suppliers or builders before the application
- Completion deadline: 1 July 2029; settlement request within 13 weeks of completion

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Projects need at least 70 of 100 points.
- Evaluation criteria and weighting: future-proof economy and climate 30; working and learning 25; employment 25; innovation and environmental quality 20
- Ranking rules: first come, first served among complete applications
